title: Swap the Bits at Even and Odd Positions

concept.title: Select the even-position bits and the odd-position bits with masks, shift them past each other, and combine
body: Number the 32 bit positions of a number from 0 at the right. Swap the bit at the position 0 with the bit at the position 1, the bit at 2 with the bit at 3, and so on: all the bits at **even** positions move one place to the **left**, and all the bits at **odd** positions move one place to the **right**. For `1 = ...0001` the result is `2 = ...0010`; for `10 = 1010` it is `5 = 0101`; for `2 = 10` it is `1`.

A *mask* selects some bits and clears the others when combined with AND. The mask `0x55555555` is `0101...0101` in binary: it has a 1 at every **even** position. The mask `0xAAAAAAAA` is `1010...1010`: it has a 1 at every **odd** position. Take the even bits `x & 0x55555555` and shift them left by one, so that they land on the odd positions; take the odd bits `x & 0xAAAAAAAA` and shift them right by one, so that they land on the even positions. The two results do not overlap, and combining them with OR gives the answer.

body.code:
for x in numbers:
    even = (x & 0x55555555) << 1
    odd = (x & 0xAAAAAAAA) >> 1
    answer.append(even | odd)
print(*answer)

body: In hexadecimal each digit `5` is `0101` and each digit `A` is `1010`, which is why the masks are so short to write. Four operations per number give O(1) time; the answer is a 32-bit number, and in C++ and Java a 64-bit type is used so that the highest bit does not turn the value negative.

statement: For each of the `q` given numbers (each smaller than 2^32), regard it as 32 bits and swap every bit at an even position (0, 2, 4, ...) with the bit just to its left (at the position one higher). Print the resulting numbers.
inputFormat: The first line has `q`: the number of questions.
outputFormat: Print `q` numbers on one line, separated by spaces.
hints: 0x55555555 has ones at the even positions and 0xAAAAAAAA at the odd positions.
Shift the even bits left by one and the odd bits right by one.
Combine the two parts with OR; use 64-bit integers.

explanation: The bits at even positions are selected with the mask 0x55555555 and shifted left by one, the bits at odd positions are selected with 0xAAAAAAAA and shifted right by one, and the two parts are combined with OR.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

q = int(input())
ns = list(map(int, input().split()))

answer = []
for x in ns:
    even = (x & 0x55555555) << 1
    odd = (x & 0xAAAAAAAA) >> 1
    answer.append(even | odd)
print(*answer)
